function: DRL jointly controls UAV trajectory, UAV radar power, IoT transmit power, offloading ratio, CPU frequency and association, minimizing offloading and sensing penalty indices (p. 7, p. 8).
system: Air-ground uplink: 2-4 UAVs with directional antennas, 10-20 IoT devices with omnidirectional antennas, OFDMA, 5.9 GHz V2I (p. 4, p. 6), fC=3.5 GHz (p. 11); no RIS.
method: Deep reinforcement learning with actor-critic networks: TD3, PPO, SAC under centralized training and execution (CTCE); SAC also under CTDE and DTDE (p. 8, p. 10, p. 11).
data_channel: Synthetic: path-loss exponent 4 with Weissberger foliage loss, two-ray sensing gain (p. 5); second scenario on Nuuksio forest geography with random device positions, no measured channel (p. 13).
test_conditions: Objective versus training iteration per setting: synthetic 2 UAVs, 10 IoT devices, 2 targets (p. 10); forest 4 UAVs, 20 IoT devices, 4 targets (p. 13); no unseen-condition test.
baselines: Learned: DDPG. Non-learned: random strategy, PSO and GA meta-heuristics. Also CTCE versus CTDE versus DTDE variants of SAC (p. 12, p. 14).
metrics: Optimization objective (weighted computation offloading and sensing penalty indices), number of successful offloading states, energy and delay, UAV trajectories; qualitative inference complexity (p. 12, p. 13, p. 15).
complexity: Big-O training complexity of SAC, TD3, PPO and big-O inference complexity of the policy network, Eqs. (31)-(36); Table III only gives Low/Medium/High (p. 10, p. 15).
q1_support: p. 5: "we take p = 4 in the forest environment" with Weissberger foliage loss; custom channel, no 3GPP or measured data; p. 13: "using real-world geographical data" only fixes the map.
q2_support: p. 14: "the curves converge at all densities, proving the scalability of the model"; p. 13: "versus the number of UAVs after 10000 iterations by SAC"; each setting is trained anew, no trained policy tested on unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 14: "we compare the proposed algorithms, i.e., TD3, SAC, and PPO with three commonly used baselines"; p. 14: "the proposed TD3, PPO, and SAC all outperform DDPG in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency"; p. 14: "The proposed algorithms outperform meta-heuristics"
q4_support: p. 10: "the complexity of inference time in centralized DRL can be approximated as" a big-O expression (Eq. 35); training-phase big-O for SAC, TD3, PPO in Eqs. (31)-(33).
q5_support: p. 13: "We further evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms using real-world geographical data"; map-based simulation with random device positions, no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Included under the rule that a work learning a physical-layer decision jointly with an above-PHY one passes above_phy: the DRL action includes IoT transmit power and UAV radar power (p. 8) with trajectory, offloading ratio and CPU frequency. Area 6 over 5 because the links are UAV air-ground links, so the single-antenna rule (p. 4) does not apply. Borderline: the objective is mostly offloading and sensing penalties, so the reviewer should confirm. Section VI real-world data is geography only (p. 13).
